rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The IUPAC system is a **reversible code** between structure and name. A name is assembled from a **word root** (meth → hex for C1 → C6), a **primary suffix** (-ane/-ene/-yne for single/double/triple bonds), **functional suffixes with locants** (-ol, -al, -one, -oic acid), and **alphabetical prefixes with locants** for substituents (di-/tri- ignored in alphabetising).…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The NEB 2023 name decoded*** — CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH(CH2CH3)CH2OH looks fearsome until the rules run: longest chain holding the OH carbon = 6 (hexan-1-ol), ethyl at C-2, methyl at C-5, alphabetical order — 2-ethyl-5-methylhexan-1-ol.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Chain length -> root; saturation -> ane/ene/yne; group position -> locant. Number from the functional-group end. Alphabetise prefixes ignoring di/tri. Practice set: butan-2-ol, butanoic acid, ethanal, ethane-1,2-diol, 2-methylpropanoic acid, 2-ethyl-5-methylhexan-1-ol.

All bonds are single → infix **-an-**. Numbering from the end nearer the **–OH** group places the hydroxyl on **C-2** → suffix **-2-ol**.…  ·  **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Give the IUPAC names of (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH (b) CH₃CHO (c) HOCH₂CH₂OH (d) CH₃CH(CH₃)COOH.** — (a) The carboxyl carbon is C-1 of a four-carbon chain → **butanoic acid**. (b) Two carbons ending in **–CHO** → **ethanal**. (c) Two carbons, each carrying an **–OH** → **ethane-1,2-diol**.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One structure must yield one name worldwide: longest chain fixes the parent, lowest locant fixes the numbering, alphabetical order fixes the listing — three rules, one unambiguous name.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: IUPAC name = prefix(es) + word root + primary suffix + functional suffix with locant. Roots: meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4, pent 5, hex 6. Suffixes: ane/ene/yne for single/double/triple bonds; -ol, -al, -one, -oic acid, -amine for groups.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: IUPAC names are constructed, not memorised: any chemist can rebuild the structure from the name alone — the system is a reversible code between words and molecules.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.  ·  ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.  ·  ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.  ·  ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).  ·  ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.  ·  ❌ pH can be negative. ✅ pH < 0 is possible for concentrations >1M (e.g., 2M HCl has pH ≈ −0.3).  ·  ❌ Kc changes when concentration changes. ✅ Kc is constant at constant temperature; only temperature changes K.
